title: Bengal limits online booking on state long-distance buses to 30% of seats
dek: The Transport Department says some free tickets for women were booked and never used, leaving buses running half-empty. The rest of the seats must now be bought at counters or on board.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
West Bengal's three state transport corporations now sell only 30% of the seats on long-distance buses online, after the Transport Department said free tickets for women under the state government's scheme were being booked in bulk and not used, according to reports. The remaining 70% must be bought at depot counters or from the conductor on boarding, subject to availability.

The change covers long-distance services of the West Bengal Transport Corporation (WBTC), the South Bengal State Transport Corporation (SBSTC) and the North Bengal State Transport Corporation (NBSTC). Each corporation issued a notice on Friday and the limit took effect on Saturday, according to reports. Some passengers who tried to book online over the weekend found no seats available, one report said.

## What changes

On a 50-seat bus, 15 seats can now be booked online and 35 are kept for counter and on-board sale, according to reports. Free tickets for women are counted within the 30% online quota. Online booking can still be made up to a month in advance, reports said. It is not clear from the reports whether shorter city and suburban routes are affected; the limit is described as applying mainly to long-distance services, such as those to Digha, north Bengal and Puri.

"30 per cent of seats will be available for advance online booking," a Transport Department official said, according to reports.

## Why the department acted

Officials say some passengers booked several free seats on more than one bus using only a name and a phone number, and then either did not travel or got off early, according to reports. As a result, buses showed as fully booked on the online system but ran with many seats empty. Fare-paying passengers who could not find seats turned to costlier private buses, and the corporations lost ticket revenue, officials said. The department has been dealing with the problem for about five months, according to reports.

"It was a good scheme, but malpractice by some people has led to this situation," a WBTC official said, according to reports. No official notice or figures on revenue losses or unused bookings have been published.

## Background

Free travel for women on state-run buses was an election promise of the BJP, which formed the state government under Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari after this year's Assembly election. It is one of the government's best-known welfare measures. The scheme itself has not been withdrawn: women can still travel free, but must now compete for a smaller pool of online seats or queue for counter tickets.

No reaction from opposition parties or from passenger groups had been reported by Monday afternoon.

## What happens next

The corporations are expected to watch how many online seats now go unused and whether counter sales recover lost revenue. A formal circular from the Transport Department, with details of which routes are covered, would settle the questions the notices left open.
